subject: [EXECSYNC] Hosted API latency surge — GPU memory degradation causing p95/p99 regressions
messages:
From: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@playlytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@playlytics.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: sudden throughput drop + 503s on /v1/generate — impacted production

Karthik,

We started seeing a spike in 5xxs and request latencies from 07:50 PDT — several of our routes to /v1/generate are returning 503s or taking >4.5s. Error rate went from ~0.3% to ~6% and p99 jumped from 420ms to ~3.6s. This is hitting user-facing inference flows for real-time scoring.

Our engineers collected a couple of sample request IDs: req_3a9f, req_3ab2, req_3c11. We also attached traces and a short recording of client体验. Can someone from Redwood confirm if there are ongoing incidents? We need an ETA — this is affecting our SLAs.

— Sarah
Product Ops, PlayLytics

Subject: Re: sudden throughput drop + 503s on /v1/generate — impacted production

Sarah — thanks for flagging. I'm escalating immediately.

Initial notes: our hosted telemetry shows a region-level p99 spike coincident with increased GPU memory churn on a subset of instance groups serving the "generation-v2" model family. We're seeing elevated OOM recovery activity and fragmentation-induced retries on the runtime. Rishi — can you start a live check of the tile mapping + kernel failures for the cluster that serves PlayLytics? Marissa, please pull the customer's recent routing policy and any canary overrides.

I'll keep you updated every 30 min.

Karthik

Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden throughput drop + 503s on /v1/generate — impacted production

Quick triage:
- Observed repeated transient OOM events on GPU nodes in us-west-2 cluster pool gw-24 between 07:40–08:30 PDT. Failure mode matches memory fragmentation where the allocator cannot satisfy large contiguous allocations for attention layers at longer context lengths.
- p95 climbed to ~1.2s and p99 to ~3.6s for the generation-v2 family for PlayLytics routes.
- Affected hosts show elevated KV cache thrash; we see per-request cache invalidations followed by warmed-but-fragmented allocations.

Immediate mitigations I recommend:
1) Route PlayLytics traffic to the standby variant of generation-v2-quant with reduced max_seq_len to avoid large contiguous allocations (rollout 10% -> 100% in 15 min windows).
2) Temporarily disable prefix prefetching / aggressive KV cache merges for that pool.
3) If the above doesn't stabilize p99 in 30–45 min, trigger an emergency scale-up of dedicated nodes (add 8x short-lived GPUs) and shift traffic.

I'll start the routing change now (canary at 10%). Logging will capture before/after metrics to the incident folder.

Rishi
Senior Runtime Engineer
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden throughput drop + 503s on /v1/generate — impacted production

Performed canary routing change at 10:05 PDT:
- 10% of PlayLytics traffic -> generation-v2-quant (reduced max_seq_len)
- Disabled aggressive prefix prefetching for the affected pool

Early effect: request p95 dropped from ~1.2s to ~850ms in the canary cohort; p99 shows small improvement but still elevated (~2.1s). No new OOMs in canary hosts so far.

Action items:
- Rishi to monitor kernel allocation failures and KV cache eviction rates over next 30 min.
- Laura to prepare executive summary for PlayLytics and ops. Include expected ETA for full mitigation (we're aiming for 2 hours).

Attaching runtime-metrics-0504.csv and kvcache-snapshot-0504.txt to the incident folder.

Marissa
Incident Lead, Runtime Reliability

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Executive brief: PlayLytics latency incident — root cause and next steps

Team — final update for execs and the PlayLytics account:
Summary:
- Impact: PlayLytics observed elevated p95/p99 and transient 503s on 2027-05-04 between ~07:40–12:30 PDT. Peak p99 ~3.6s.
- Root cause: GPU memory fragmentation in the runtime allocator on a subset of us-west-2 hosts combined with aggressive KV cache prefetching on long-context requests. This caused transient OOMs and allocation failures that triggered retries and longer tail latencies.
- Customer impact: real-time scoring degraded; PlayLytics reported increased error rate and SLA risk. No customer data exposure identified.

Actions taken:
- Canary reroute to a quantized model variant with reduced max_seq_len; disabled aggressive prefix prefetching (rolled 10% -> 100% within 90 minutes).
- Short-lived capacity bump (6 GPUs) provisioned to absorb pressure while allocator defrag heuristics are tuned.
- Telemetry alerts updated to include allocator fragmentation ratio and per-model kvcache eviction spikes.
- Customer communications: Laura prepared an incident summary and proposed credit options; Karthik to coordinate exec-facing call.

Follow-ups (owners):
- Rishi: implement allocator defragmentation signals + emergency fallback trigger (ETA 2 weeks).
- Marissa: postmortem draft and runbook updates for fragmentation OOMs (ETA 5 business days).
- Laura: finalize customer-facing letter and credit calculation (ETA EOD tomorrow).
- Tessa: update Redwood Console dashboard to show fragmentation metrics near model family and route-level granularity (ETA 10 days).

Notes for Execs: we should consider making the reduced contiguous-allocation variant an automated fallback for any customer with >1000 r/s peaks to avoid recurrence. Recommendation: brief the product and infra budget owners for a small Q3 effort to harden allocator heuristics.

I'll schedule a 30-min exec sync tomorrow at 09:30 PDT to align on credits and customer messaging.

Karthik
Director, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
